decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The Council of the London Borough of Hounslow has considered the Consultation Scoping Report and raises no objection provided that the scope of the proposed Environmental Impact Assessment is modified to take account of the following:

Ground Conditions:

Given the scale of the site, the potential level of contamination and the possibility of such material migrating off-site, The London Borough of Hounslow should be consulted at every stage of the assessment of the ground conditions and waste. Hounslow should be identified as a statutory consultee in respect of this. 

Water Environment:

This section needs to make it explicit as to what it relates to - it should include man-made water courses such as the Grand Union Canal and the appropriate statutory consultees should be consulted.

Transport:

The scale of the development is likely to have a harmful effect on the London Borough of Hounslow's roads, particularly at Hayes Road. The transport assessment will need to include part of the Borough in the detailed modelling exercise and as such a study boundary should be agreed with the London Borough of Hounslow, prior to commencement. 

Landscape and Visual:

Locations within  Hounslow Borough should also be included a representative receptors for the landscape and visual impact assessment.

Air Quality:

There needs to be a stronger link between the air quality and transport assessment of the impacts of the development. With reference to paragraph 3.6.4 it is essential that the London Borough of Hounslow is consulted and an agreement reached for the methodology describing the detailed approach and assumptions that would apply for the assessment.

Ecology & Nature Conservation:

Hounslow Borough should be consulted about ecology and nature conservation, not least due to the site's proximity to the Grand Union Canal.  Paragraph 3.8.3, should also refer to Hounslow's Biodiversity Action Plan.
